newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers stake in clothes firm Kabo.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers stake in clothes firm Kabo.

text.p: Egypt's state-owned Holding Company for Spinning and Weaving on Tuesday offered investors at least 10 percent of its stake in partially private Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles.

The company said in a published announcement that investors could buy the 306,200 shares from Wednesday, May 28 to the end of Thursday, May 29. The minimum bidding price is the closing price of the stock at the end of trading on Monday, which was 109 pounds.
Investors can buy a minimum of 5,000 shares. The Commercial Bank of Egypt and its Commercial International Investment Company are the agents for the sale.

Kabo's total equity is divided into a total 3.06 million shares. The holding company owns a 70.05 percent stake and private investors the remaining 29.95 percent. The firm manufactures garments under its own label and for several international brands like JIL, Jockey, British Home Stores and Wrangler.
The firm said in the statement it had sold goods worth 135.75 million pounds in the past 1995/6 financial year compared to 151.91 million in 1994/5. The years end on June 30.
After-tax profits in 1995/6 were slightly higher at 22.761 million compared to 22.308 million in 94/5. Dividends were also higher at four pounds compared to three pounds.
The statement showed long-term assets in 1995/6 were worth 21.063 million pounds compared to 19.671 million in 94/5 while current assets rose to 198.291 million from 181.941 million.
Current liabilities were valued at 80.431 million in 95/6 while in 94/5 they were 70.303 million.
Total investments rose to 138.923 million from 131.309 million in 94/5.

The privatisation is part of a spate of government sell-offs in the past two weeks. The state has promised investors to accelerate the privatisation programme which is the flagship of its economic reforms.
